searchText: Tuesday isn't over yet, <@291925846556540928> still has time to finish authoring the blog post. 😄 I would push back pretty hard on delaying the merge because a single client has a bug. People can run any of the other clients, and it being the majority client that currently has a bug just makes it all that much better as it gives people a push to stop using the majority client. makes one think if that was planned :P I strongly disagree, a lot of enterprises use their own node forks to suit their business needs Replacing a node is not a trivial task to do in this case That is no excuse for continuing to compromise the network with a majority client. We have been telling people to switch away from Geth for a long time. At this point "it is hard" is not a legitimate excuse. You know, there is a decent reason why people prefer using Geth over anything else Geth is just the best one out in the market, and it is the most stable node. Also the fact that it is written in Go makes its UX a lot better. doesn't look very stable Since the last update, yes 😅 but it is a bug that is being fixed by developers right, so its probably better to use multiple nodes if you want stability Scroll up This right, so its their task to maintain them :) Also IMO Ethereum should work on incentivizing people to switch their nodes, rather than punishing them if they use Geth There isn't really anything we can do to incentivize or punish other than at the social layer. And of course, introducing bugs into majority clients. 😆 I mean this why does Go improve UX? I tried using Nethermind, but there are quite a few features unimplemented. Plus, the devops experience is almost non-existent — I remember making a docker image for it and it was 100x harder than what it is with Geth Erigon still advertises that it is alpha software and that it should not be used in production (that’s a red flag for every enterprise) right, so Erigon is working on that? :P Besu has a **lot** of features unimplemented, and it is written in Java which makes devops as bad as it is with Nethermind Yes, they do But Micah tells us to switch from Geth now, not sometimes in the future right, those clients get better when more people are working with them I’m not sure what do you mean by saying this here? when I work with minority node, I maybe have to develop something extra when using it, which I can share, I also find some bugs that I can report to devs etc Ah, yes that’s true But very unlikely enterprises will do that 😅 there's many things enterprises won't do, and it's their problem :) If you say that every problem running the node is the problem of the person who is doing that, I don’t think that we should continue continue this discussion. I don't know how you got that from my reply 🤔 I think if you overly generalize everything I say, I guess this discussion is not gonna work either Nethermind is shipped in Docker form. You can just start from that. I actually don't remember in full, it was either a docker image or I was setting it up on a machine locally. All I remember is a deadly mess with .NET SDK and RocksDB DLLs 😅 It's not like Geth where everything is bundled into a single binary
